subsystems.name: Detector network
subsystems.role: measures the tiny stretching of space produced by a passing gravitational wave.
parts: kilometre-scale laser interferometers with suspended mirrors

subsystems.name: Continuous-wave search stack
subsystems.role: hunts for long-lived, nearly monochromatic signals rather than short chirps.
parts: Doppler correction for Earth's rotation and orbit

subsystems.name: Transient and burst searches
subsystems.role: catches short exotic events that do not match known merger waveforms.

subsystems.name: Astrophysical population models
subsystems.role: defines what ordinary black holes and neutron stars can produce, so anything outside that box stands out.

subsystems.name: Follow-up network
subsystems.role: checks whether a gravitational candidate has any electromagnetic or neutrino counterpart.

subsystems.name: Vetting and injection pipeline
subsystems.role: separates real signals from instrumental artefacts.

buildSteps.title: Define the engineered signal class
buildSteps.detail: Theory work first: decide what a technological source could look like — a slowly spinning compact object emitting a nearly pure tone, a binary with unnatural masses or spins, or a chirp that stops or repeats instead of merging away.

buildSteps.title: Model the waveform
buildSteps.detail: Turn that idea into a mathematical template, including how the signal would be modulated by the detector's daily rotation and yearly orbit around the Sun.

buildSteps.title: Set the search band
buildSteps.detail: Choose frequency ranges and sky positions where detector noise is lowest and known instrumental lines are avoided.

buildSteps.title: Filter the data
buildSteps.detail: Slide each template through months of interferometer strain data, summing signal-to-noise coherently across the detector network.

buildSteps.title: Estimate the background
buildSteps.detail: Repeat the search on time-shifted data, where the detectors cannot be seeing the same event, to measure how often noise alone produces a candidate.

buildSteps.title: Vet candidates
buildSteps.detail: Re-examine any excess against instrumental lines, calibration signals, seismic and magnetic records, and require it to appear consistently in independent detectors.

buildSteps.title: Run blind injections
buildSteps.detail: Deliberately add simulated artificial signals into the live data stream and confirm the pipeline recovers them at the expected strength.

buildSteps.title: Cross-check other messengers
buildSteps.detail: Trigger optical, radio and neutrino follow-up at the candidate's sky position; a counterpart strengthens the case but its absence does not rule out a source.

buildSteps.title: Publish limits and archive
buildSteps.detail: Release upper limits on engineered sources and keep the candidate list for re-analysis as detector sensitivity improves.

prerequisites.why: without strain data there is no search; several detectors are now observing in coordinated runs.
months-long coherent searches need large, well-tested matched-filter codebases.
we know compact-binary masses and rates reasonably well, but not every natural formation channel, so an anomaly is hard to prove.

prerequisites.tech: A worked-out theory of engineered gravitational-wave sources
prerequisites.why: nobody can yet say what a technological emitter would predictably look like, so searches must stay very generic.
current sensitivity reaches only nearby sources at these frequencies, greatly limiting the volume that can be surveyed.

pathway.milestone: continuous observing runs with several interferometers; upper limits on long-lived monochromatic emission
pathway.unlocks: a growing catalogue of known astrophysical signals to compare against.

pathway.milestone: pulsar-timing arrays reporting a nanohertz background, plus improved interferometer sensitivity
pathway.unlocks: a second, much lower-frequency window on exotic and possibly artificial sources.

pathway.milestone: space-based interferometry in the millihertz band, planned for the 2030s
pathway.unlocks: sensitivity to source classes no ground detector can see, including very long-lived orbits.

pathway.milestone: next-generation ground interferometers with far greater reach
pathway.unlocks: large enough surveyed volume that a null result becomes a meaningful limit on technological emitters.
